steps.path: Any file open in the file viewer, in Comments mode
steps.headline: This is what done means for document comments.

rows.statement: Word and Excel files keep their comments inside the file; every other file's comments live in a hidden project folder.
rows.threshold: opening the file in Word, Excel, or the project's hidden folder shows the comments, in a dev instance
rows.note: Settles the note on Q-1 asking that formats able to hold comments natively store them there instead.

rows.statement: The assistant can reply to your comments right where you left them.
The assistant can resolve a comment once it finishes what you asked; reopening one takes a single click.
The assistant leaves its own comments only sparingly, on things that clearly need your attention, never to narrate its own work.
rows.note: Settles the note on Q-2 limiting how freely the assistant may add its own comments.

rows.statement: The assistant can edit a file to fix what a comment asks, following its existing edit-approval rules.
After fixing a comment, the assistant decides whether to reply, resolve, or move it to the new wording; nothing is silently lost.
rows.note: Settles the note on Q-2 about what happens to a comment once the assistant edits the text it pointed at.

rows.statement: On a phone, tapping a highlighted or commented cell slides that comment up from the bottom of the screen.
Spreadsheet comments attach to a specific cell and are saved into the spreadsheet file itself.
rows.threshold: opening the spreadsheet in Excel shows the same cell comments, in a dev instance

rows.statement: Word comments work both ways: comments made in Word or Google Docs show here, and comments you add here show there.
rows.threshold: replying in YouCoded to a colleague's Word comment shows the reply in Word, in a dev instance

rows.statement: Opening a commented Word file in Google Docs keeps its comments; a live Google Drive link comes later.
rows.threshold: uploading a commented Word file to Google Drive keeps the comments, in a dev instance

rows.statement: The July draft pull request (#263) for the earlier attempt is closed on GitHub, pointing to this work.
Comments show as highlights in the text; hovering one shows a card to reply or resolve, and clicking opens the full panel.
Selecting text or right-clicking opens the same menu; Add comment opens a small box next to your selection.
Show Resolved sits at the top of the comment panel, under the title, and an X in the top corner closes the panel.
Ask about this puts a chip in your sentence; hovering it lights up its source, and clicking scrolls to it, even after sending.
Ask Your Assistant sends one summary chip naming the comment count and file, instead of one chip per comment.
rows.note: Settles the review note that one chip per comment was probably not the way to go.

rows.statement: Word and spreadsheet files show the same comment panel; colleagues' Word comments appear under their name, and commented cells get a red corner mark.
Code files use the same comment panel, and Ask about this chips from code light up their lines.
On the Projects screen, Comments is a header button beside the file's other actions, with the same panel and Ask Your Assistant.
From Projects, Ask Your Assistant opens a new-chat pop-up with the file's project already chosen and a model to pick.
rows.note: Settles the review note asking for a model-picking pop-up, the same one Create a page uses.

rows.statement: The three rejected practice branches and folders no longer exist, on GitHub or on this computer.
